PRIVILEGED & CONFIDENTIAL — ATTORNEY WORK PRODUCT
MEMORANDUM
TO: File — Nexford Industrial Holdings Inc. / Pinnacle Metal Fabricators LLC Asset Acquisition
FROM: Naomi Petersen and Ryan Kowalski, Calderwood & Harkness LLP
REVIEWED BY: Oliver Mackenzie, Partner, Calderwood & Harkness LLP
DATE: October 24, 2023
RE: Deal Summary Memorandum — Asset Acquisition of Substantially All Assets of Pinnacle Metal Fabricators LLC by Nexford Industrial Holdings Inc.
Matter No.: 1005-00006
Right-click to update Table of Contents
I. Executive Summary
This memorandum is an internal document prepared by Calderwood & Harkness LLP for purposes of summarizing the key deal terms, material diligence findings, identified risk factors, and closing mechanics in connection with the completed asset acquisition of substantially all of the assets of Pinnacle Metal Fabricators LLC by Nexford Industrial Holdings Inc. This memorandum is intended solely for the use of the Calderwood & Harkness LLP deal team and, as appropriate, the client and its private equity sponsor, Bramblewood Capital Partners, LP. This memorandum is protected by the attorney-client privilege and constitutes attorney work product.
Buyer. Nexford Industrial Holdings Inc. ("Nexford" or "NIH") is a Delaware corporation headquartered at 4200 West Lake Shore Drive, Suite 800, Chicago, Illinois 60604. Nexford operates as a diversified manufacturing platform focused on precision metals, engineered components, and specialty fabrication, generating last-twelve-months ("LTM") revenue of approximately $285 million across six operating subsidiaries. Nexford is majority-owned by Bramblewood Capital Partners, LP ("Bramblewood" or "BCP"), a Chicago-based middle-market private equity fund, which holds approximately 78% of Nexford's equity. The Bramblewood deal partner responsible for the Nexford platform is Catherine E. Moreau, who serves as a Board Observer.
Seller. Pinnacle Metal Fabricators LLC ("Pinnacle" or "PMF") is an Indiana limited liability company located at 1127 Industrial Parkway, Hammond, Indiana 46320. Founded in 2006 by Gerald T. Brennan, Pinnacle is a custom metal fabrication business specializing in structural steel, aluminum, and stainless-steel components for commercial construction, infrastructure, and industrial OEM end-markets. As of the twelve months ended June 30, 2023, Pinnacle generated revenue of approximately $18.4 million and Adjusted EBITDA of approximately $3.7 million, representing a 20.1% Adjusted EBITDA margin. Pinnacle employs 74 full-time employees.
Transaction Type. The transaction was structured as an asset purchase, pursuant to which Nexford acquired substantially all of the assets of Pinnacle, subject to the assumption of certain specified liabilities. The definitive Asset Purchase Agreement (the "APA") is governed by New York law.
Purchase Price. The total purchase price for the transaction was $30,000,000, consisting of (i) a closing cash payment of $24,000,000 and (ii) a performance-based earnout of up to $6,000,000, payable in two installments over two twelve-month post-closing measurement periods, contingent on the achievement of specified EBITDA targets. Of the $24,000,000 closing cash payment, $3,000,000 was deposited into an indemnification escrow account held by Commonwealth Escrow Services Inc., resulting in net closing cash to the Seller members of $21,000,000.
Implied Valuation. On total consideration (assuming full earnout achievement), the transaction implies a valuation of approximately 8.1x LTM Adjusted EBITDA ($30,000,000 ÷ $3,700,000). On closing cash consideration alone, the implied valuation is approximately 6.5x LTM Adjusted EBITDA ($24,000,000 ÷ $3,700,000). These multiples are consistent with recent comparable transactions in the specialty metals fabrication sector and reflect the premium associated with Pinnacle's strong margin profile, established customer relationships, and strategic positioning in Midwest infrastructure end-markets.
Timeline and Closing. The engagement was opened and the Letter of Intent was executed on July 11, 2023. The exclusivity period ran from July 11, 2023 through September 15, 2023, a period of approximately 66 days. Due diligence was substantially completed by August 25, 2023. The APA was executed on September 5, 2023. The transaction closed on October 24, 2023, four days after the original target closing date of October 20, 2023, due to a delay in obtaining final title clearance on certain equipment included in the Acquired Assets.
Counsel. Calderwood & Harkness LLP served as buyer's counsel throughout the transaction. Halverson Burke & Crane LLP (Thomas A. Gilroy, lead partner) served as seller's counsel.
Strategic Rationale. The Pinnacle acquisition extends Nexford's manufacturing capabilities into heavy-gauge structural steel and aluminum fabrication for Midwest infrastructure end-markets, a segment that complements Nexford's existing precision metals and engineered components businesses. The acquisition represents the fifth tuck-in acquisition completed by Nexford since Bramblewood's acquisition of the platform in 2019, consistent with Nexford's disciplined buy-and-build strategy.
II. Parties
A. Buyer — Nexford Industrial Holdings Inc.
Nexford Industrial Holdings Inc. is a corporation duly organized and existing under the laws of the State of Delaware. Its Employer Identification Number is 84-3291047. Nexford maintains its principal executive offices at 4200 West Lake Shore Drive, Suite 800, Chicago, Illinois 60604.
Nexford operates as a diversified manufacturing platform focused on precision metals, engineered components, and specialty fabrication. The company generates LTM revenue of approximately $285 million across six operating subsidiaries, each of which serves distinct but complementary end-markets within the broader industrial and manufacturing sectors. Nexford's executive leadership team includes Marcus R. Haverford, Chief Executive Officer; Danielle K. Cho, Chief Financial Officer; and Philip M. Stanhope, General Counsel.
Since Bramblewood Capital Partners' acquisition of the Nexford platform in 2019, the company has pursued a disciplined buy-and-build strategy, completing four tuck-in acquisitions prior to the Pinnacle transaction. These acquisitions have expanded Nexford's geographic footprint, broadened its manufacturing capabilities, and deepened its presence in key end-markets. The Pinnacle acquisition represents the fifth such tuck-in and extends Nexford's capabilities into heavy-gauge structural steel and aluminum fabrication for Midwest infrastructure end-markets, an area of strategic importance given the anticipated increase in infrastructure spending across the region.
B. Seller — Pinnacle Metal Fabricators LLC and Its Members
Pinnacle Metal Fabricators LLC is a limited liability company duly organized and existing under the laws of the State of Indiana. Its Employer Identification Number is 27-1684352. Pinnacle's entity identification number with the Indiana Secretary of State is 2006041500237. Its registered agent is Hoosier Registered Agents Inc., located at 201 South Capitol Avenue, Indianapolis, Indiana 46225.
Pinnacle was founded in 2006 by Gerald T. Brennan, a veteran of the structural metals industry with over 30 years of experience in custom metal fabrication, project management, and client development. Since its founding, Pinnacle has established itself as a reliable provider of custom metal fabrication services, specializing in structural steel, aluminum, and stainless-steel components for commercial construction, infrastructure, and industrial OEM customers. As of the twelve months ended June 30, 2023, Pinnacle generated revenue of approximately $18.4 million and Adjusted EBITDA of approximately $3.7 million, representing a 20.1% Adjusted EBITDA margin. The company employs 74 full-time employees, comprising 42 shop floor personnel, 18 field installation personnel, and 14 office and management staff.
The members of Pinnacle, together with their respective membership interests and roles, are as follows:
Gerald "Gerry" T. Brennan — Managing Member, holding a 65% membership interest. Mr. Brennan is the founder of Pinnacle and has served as its Managing Member since inception. He has over 30 years of experience in the structural metals industry and maintains deep relationships with Pinnacle's key customers. Pursuant to the Transition Services Agreement described in Section VIII below, Mr. Brennan will serve as a transition consultant to Nexford for a period of 12 months following the closing.
Sandra L. Brennan — Member, holding a 20% membership interest. Ms. Brennan is the spouse of Gerald Brennan and has served in a bookkeeping and office administration capacity for Pinnacle. Ms. Brennan was not retained by Nexford following the closing but is subject to certain restrictive covenants as described in Section VIII below.
Derek J. Kopp — Member, holding a 15% membership interest. Mr. Kopp has served as Pinnacle's Vice President of Operations since 2012 and oversees day-to-day shop floor operations, production scheduling, and quality control. Mr. Kopp has been retained by Nexford as Plant Manager pursuant to an employment agreement described in Section VIII below.
C. Sponsor — Bramblewood Capital Partners, LP
Bramblewood Capital Partners, LP is a Delaware limited partnership with its principal office located at 200 South Wacker Drive, Suite 3100, Chicago, Illinois 60606. Bramblewood is a middle-market private equity fund focused on investments in the industrials, business services, and specialty distribution sectors.
Bramblewood's Fund III, with total committed capital of approximately $1.2 billion, is the investment vehicle through which Bramblewood holds its interest in Nexford. The Managing Partner of Bramblewood is Liam S. Ashford. The Deal Partner responsible for the Nexford platform investment is Catherine E. Moreau, who serves as a Board Observer on the Nexford board of directors. Bramblewood acquired Nexford in 2019 for an enterprise value of approximately $190 million and currently holds approximately 78% of Nexford's equity.
Throughout the Pinnacle acquisition process, Ms. Moreau was actively involved in deal evaluation, diligence oversight, and purchase price negotiations. Bramblewood's investment thesis for the Pinnacle acquisition centered on the opportunity to expand Nexford's addressable market into heavy-gauge structural steel and aluminum fabrication for infrastructure end-markets, an area benefiting from favorable secular tailwinds, including anticipated federal and state infrastructure spending programs.
D. Advisors and Counterparties
The following advisors and counterparties were engaged in connection with the transaction:
Buyer's Counsel: Calderwood & Harkness LLP. The deal team consisted of Oliver Mackenzie (Responsible Partner), Harrison Wexford (Billing Partner), Naomi Petersen (Lead Associate), and Ryan Kowalski (Working Associate). The firm's address is 120 South LaSalle Street, Suite 4500, Chicago, Illinois 60603.
Seller's Counsel: Halverson Burke & Crane LLP. The lead partner was Thomas A. Gilroy, with Jessica N. Farrow serving as associate counsel. Halverson Burke & Crane represented the Seller and its members in connection with all aspects of the transaction, including negotiation of the APA, disclosure schedules, ancillary agreements, and closing deliverables.
Buyer's Lender: Greystone National Bank, N.A. The primary contact was Andrew F. Liang, Relationship Manager, who coordinated the lender consent process and the revolver draw at closing.
Escrow Agent: Commonwealth Escrow Services Inc. The primary contact was Margaret H. Velasquez. Commonwealth Escrow Services holds the $3,000,000 indemnification escrow pursuant to the terms of the Escrow Agreement dated October 24, 2023.
Financial Diligence Advisor: Whitfield & Pryor LLP. Robert C. Underhill served as Engagement Partner and oversaw the quality-of-earnings analysis and working capital assessment performed in connection with the transaction.
Environmental Consultant: Clearpath Environmental Advisors Inc. Elena M. Rivas served as Project Manager for the Phase I Environmental Site Assessment of the Pinnacle facility at 1127 Industrial Parkway, Hammond, Indiana.
R&W Insurance Broker: Ashford & Meridian Insurance Brokers LLC. Nathan R. Caldwell served as the primary broker in procuring the representations and warranties insurance policy for the transaction.
R&W Insurance Carrier: Sentinel Specialty Insurance Company. The policy was issued under Policy Number SSI-RW-1032-00004 and provides coverage for breaches of representations and warranties made by the Seller in the APA.
Earnout Dispute Accountant: Calder & Fitch LLP, Indianapolis, Indiana. To be engaged in the event that a dispute arises with respect to the calculation of earnout payments under the APA. Calder & Fitch has been pre-agreed by the parties as the independent accounting firm for purposes of the earnout dispute resolution mechanism.
III. Deal Structure and Purchase Price
A. Transaction Type
The transaction was structured as an asset purchase, pursuant to which Nexford acquired substantially all of the assets of Pinnacle in exchange for the purchase price described below. The transaction was not structured as a purchase of membership interests or other equity interests in Pinnacle. Because the transaction was structured as an asset purchase at the entity level, no Section 338(h)(10) election was required or applicable; Nexford receives a stepped-up tax basis in the acquired assets by operation of the asset purchase structure itself. The APA and all ancillary agreements are governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of New York, without regard to conflicts-of-law principles that would result in the application of the laws of any other jurisdiction.
B. Acquired Assets
Pursuant to Section 2.01 of the APA, Nexford acquired substantially all of the assets of Pinnacle, including, without limitation, the following categories of tangible and intangible assets:
(a) Equipment. All CNC plasma and laser cutting equipment (14 machines in total), together with two overhead bridge cranes, all associated tooling, fixtures, and accessories. These assets constitute the core production equipment of Pinnacle's fabrication operations and were inspected as part of the diligence process.
(b) Rolling Stock. Eight flatbed trucks used for the transportation and delivery of fabricated components, together with three forklifts used in the shop floor and yard operations.
(c) Inventory. All raw materials and work-in-process inventory on hand as of the closing date. The inventory was valued for purposes of the closing working capital adjustment at levels consistent with Pinnacle's historical accounting practices.
(d) Customer Contracts and Backlog. All customer contracts, purchase orders, and associated backlog,

PRIVILEGED & CONFIDENTIAL — ATTORNEY WORK PRODUCT
CALDERWOOD & HARKNESS LLP 600 Lexington Avenue, 30th Floor New York, NY 10022
Matter No.: 1006-00006
To: Deal Team — Harrison Wexford (Partner), Beatrice Holloway (Partner), Derek Okonkwo (Associate), Leonard Cross (Partner, Tax)
From: Megan Chu (Associate)
Date: May 2, 2025
Re: Deal Summary Memorandum — Crestline Packaging Solutions LLC — Acquisition of Substantially All Assets of Allegheny Valley Packaging, Inc.
Right-click to update Table of Contents
I. Executive Summary
This memorandum summarizes the material terms, structure, parties, financing, and key diligence considerations in connection with the proposed acquisition by Crestline Packaging Solutions LLC ("Crestline" or "CPS"), an Ohio limited liability company and portfolio company of Ridgeway Capital Partners Fund III, LP ("Ridgeway" or the "Sponsor"), of substantially all of the assets of Allegheny Valley Packaging, Inc. ("AVP" or the "Seller"), a Pennsylvania corporation (S-corporation for federal income tax purposes), for an aggregate purchase price of One Hundred Eighty Million Dollars ($180,000,000) (the "Purchase Price"). The transaction is structured as an asset purchase and will be governed by an Asset Purchase Agreement (the "APA") to be governed by New York law.
AVP is a family-owned regional corrugated and specialty packaging manufacturer headquartered in Butler, Pennsylvania, with a secondary manufacturing facility in Meadville, Pennsylvania. AVP has trailing twelve-month ("TTM") revenue of approximately $95,000,000 and TTM adjusted EBITDA of approximately $18,500,000. At the stated Purchase Price of $180,000,000, the transaction implies an enterprise value to adjusted EBITDA multiple of approximately 9.7x ($180,000,000 ÷ $18,500,000 ≈ 9.73x).
The acquisition constitutes a bolt-on addition to Crestline's existing manufacturing footprint, which currently comprises six plants located across Ohio, Indiana, and Kentucky, employing approximately 1,400 employees and generating TTM revenue of approximately $620,000,000. Crestline was acquired by Ridgeway Capital Partners Fund III, LP in 2021 for approximately $475,000,000 and has since completed two prior bolt-on acquisitions, making the AVP acquisition its third bolt-on transaction under Ridgeway ownership.
Calderwood & Harkness LLP represents Crestline as buyer's counsel. The engagement letter was signed on April 1, 2025, and the matter was formally opened on April 8, 2025. A letter of intent ("LOI") was executed on April 10, 2025, which includes a 60-day exclusivity period expiring on June 9, 2025. The estimated APA execution date is June 15, 2025, with an estimated Closing Date of July 31, 2025. The outside date (or "drop-dead date") under the APA is September 30, 2025.
Based on the applicable threshold analysis following asset carve-out review, a filing under the Hart-Scott-Rodino Antitrust Improvements Act of 1976, as amended (the "HSR Act"), is not required. A separate HSR Act Analysis Memorandum is being prepared to memorialize this conclusion.
On the sell side, Veltrano Hargrave & Co. (Warren T. Blackwell, Managing Director) acted as AVP's investment banker and ran a limited sale process, through which Crestline was contacted as a strategic buyer.
The Purchase Price will be funded through a combination of (a) a $130,000,000 incremental term loan under Crestline's existing credit agreement (Amendment No. 3), with Pinnacle National Bank, N.A. serving as Administrative Agent and Lead Arranger, and (b) a $50,000,000 equity contribution from Ridgeway Capital Partners Fund III, LP, pursuant to an equity commitment letter dated April 22, 2025.
Key transaction features and risk considerations are discussed in detail throughout this memorandum and include, among other matters: (i) an environmental Recognized Environmental Condition ("REC") at the Butler facility involving trichloroethylene ("TCE") contamination, with preliminary remediation cost estimates of $1,200,000 to $2,800,000, covered by an $8,000,000 environmental special indemnity from Seller; (ii) a collective bargaining agreement with International Paperworkers Union Local 814 covering approximately 185 hourly employees, which Crestline will assume as a successor employer; (iii) customer concentration, with the top 10 customers representing approximately 62% of TTM revenue; (iv) sales and use tax exposure of approximately $420,000 across three jurisdictions (PA, OH, WV); and (v) underfunded pension obligations of approximately $3,100,000, which will be treated as Excluded Liabilities.
This memorandum is intended to serve as a comprehensive reference for the deal team and should be read in conjunction with the various sub-memoranda and analyses referenced herein.
II. Parties and Key Personnel
A. Buyer — Crestline Packaging Solutions LLC
Full Legal Name: Crestline Packaging Solutions LLC
Entity Type: Ohio limited liability company
Headquarters: 4100 Commerce Parkway, Suite 800, Akron, OH 44308
Registered Agent: Capitol Statutory Services Inc., 65 East Ashbury Asset Advisors, Columbus, OH 43215
Ohio Secretary of State Filing No.: 4287653
Federal Employer Identification Number (EIN): 84-3291047
Key Officers and Personnel:
•  Chief Executive Officer: Thomas R. Garner
•  Chief Financial Officer: Priya Mehta
•  General Counsel: Sandra K. Liu
Business Description: Crestline is a mid-market manufacturer of corrugated packaging, industrial containers, and specialty chemical-resistant packaging materials. The company currently operates six manufacturing plants located in Ohio, Indiana, and Kentucky, and employs approximately 1,400 individuals across its platform. CPS has generated TTM revenue of approximately $620,000,000. Crestline was acquired by Ridgeway Capital Partners Fund III, LP in 2021 for approximately $475,000,000 and has subsequently completed two bolt-on acquisitions prior to the contemplated AVP transaction. The AVP acquisition would represent CPS's third bolt-on and would expand its geographic footprint into western Pennsylvania while adding complementary product capabilities in folding cartons and specialty coatings.
B. Sponsor — Ridgeway Capital Partners Fund III, LP
Full Legal Name: Ridgeway Capital Partners Fund III, LP
Entity Type: Delaware limited partnership
General Partner: Ridgeway Capital GP III LLC, a Delaware limited liability company
Principal Office: 277 Park Avenue, 38th Floor, New York, NY 10172
Federal Employer Identification Number (EIN): 83-2107594
Managing Partners: Julian C. Adler and Francesca DiNardo
Background: Ridgeway Capital Partners is a private equity firm focused on middle-market industrial and specialty manufacturing businesses. Fund III held its final close in 2020 at aggregate capital commitments of $2.8 billion. Ridgeway's investment thesis centers on acquiring market-leading platforms in niche industrial verticals and pursuing value creation through operational improvement and strategic bolt-on acquisitions. Crestline represents one of Fund III's core platform investments.
Role in the Transaction: Ridgeway is the indirect parent and equity sponsor of Crestline. Ridgeway is not a party to the APA. However, Ridgeway will provide the following in connection with the transaction:
•  Equity Commitment Letter: Dated April 22, 2025, committing $50,000,000 to CPS for purposes of funding a portion of the Purchase Price. Subject to customary conditions including execution of the definitive APA and satisfaction of closing conditions therein.
•  Limited Guarantee: Ridgeway Capital Partners Fund III, LP (acting by its general partner, Ridgeway Capital GP III LLC) will deliver a limited guarantee in favor of AVP guaranteeing certain payment obligations of CPS under the APA, including the reverse termination fee. The scope and terms of the limited guarantee are under negotiation and will be finalized in connection with the APA.
C. Seller — Allegheny Valley Packaging, Inc.
Full Legal Name: Allegheny Valley Packaging, Inc.
Entity Type: Pennsylvania corporation (S-corporation for federal income tax purposes)
Headquarters: 250 Industrial Boulevard, Butler, PA 16001
Registered Agent: Keystone Corporate Services LLC, 1500 Market Street, Suite 3500, Philadelphia, PA 19102
Pennsylvania Department of State Entity ID: 6519847
Federal Employer Identification Number (EIN): 25-1784632
Key Officers, Directors, and Shareholders:
•  President / Founder: Gerald W. Horvath (age 68; 72% shareholder). Mr. Horvath founded AVP in 1987 and has served as its President since inception. Mr. Horvath intends to retire following the closing of the transaction. He will be subject to a Non-Competition and Non-Solicitation Agreement.
•  Vice President, Operations: Michael G. Horvath (age 41; son of Gerald W. Horvath; 10% shareholder). Michael Horvath is expected to continue as a key employee of Crestline following the closing and will enter into a Consulting Agreement to support post-closing transition, as well as a separate Non-Competition and Non-Solicitation Agreement.
•  Director / Shareholder: Patricia A. Horvath (spouse of Gerald W. Horvath; 18% shareholder). Mrs. Horvath holds an 18% equity stake in AVP and serves as a member of the Board of Directors but does not hold an active operational role.
•  Controller: Diane L. Pulaski. Ms. Pulaski is AVP's principal accounting officer and has served in this capacity for approximately 12 years. She has been the primary contact for financial diligence requests and coordinated with AVP's auditors, Pendleton & Sawyer CPAs LLP.
Business Description: AVP is a family-owned manufacturer of corrugated packaging, folding cartons, and specialty coatings for food-grade and chemical-grade packaging applications. The company operates two manufacturing facilities — its primary plant in Butler, Pennsylvania, and a secondary facility in Meadville, Pennsylvania — and employs approximately 340 individuals. Key products include corrugated containers, folding cartons, specialty chemical-resistant coatings, and food-grade packaging materials. AVP has TTM revenue of approximately $95,000,000 and TTM adjusted EBITDA of approximately $18,500,000. The company's top 10 customers account for approximately 62% of TTM revenue. AVP's principal raw material input is containerboard, which is principally sourced from Consolidated Linerboard Corp. pursuant to a long-term supply agreement.
D. Advisors and Key Third Parties
The following table summarizes the advisors and key third parties involved in the transaction:

III. Transaction Structure
The transaction is structured as an asset purchase pursuant to which Crestline will acquire substantially all of the assets of AVP, and assume certain specified liabilities, pursuant to the APA. The APA will be governed by the laws of the State of New York. Crestline is the Buyer and AVP is the Seller under the APA. As noted above, this transaction represents the third bolt-on acquisition by Crestline since its acquisition by Ridgeway in 2021, following two prior bolt-on transactions that have expanded Crestline's manufacturing capacity and product offerings.
The decision to structure the transaction as an asset purchase rather than a stock acquisition was driven by several considerations, including: (a) the ability to select and exclude certain liabilities (including pre-closing indebtedness, underfunded pension obligations, and pre-closing product liability claims); (b) the potential for a stepped-up tax basis in the acquired assets; (c) AVP's status as an S-corporation, which means gain on an asset sale is recognized at the shareholder level and passed through, eliminating the double-taxation concern that would otherwise weigh in favor of a stock deal for a C-corporation seller; and (d) the Buyer's ability to undertake targeted environmental and operational diligence on the specific assets being acquired. Additional analysis regarding the tax implications of the asset purchase structure is set forth in the Tax Structure Memorandum prepared by Leonard Cross.
A. Acquired Assets
The Acquired Assets under the APA include substantially all assets of AVP used in or related to the conduct of AVP's business, including without limitation:
Real Property. The two manufacturing facilities owned by AVP, consisting of:
•  Butler Plant (Primary Facility): 250 Industrial Boulevard, Butler, PA 16001. The Butler Plant comprises approximately 285,000 square feet of manufacturing, warehouse, and office space situated on approximately 22.5 acres. This is AVP's headquarters and primary production facility.
•  Meadville Plant (Secondary Facility): 1480 Conneaut Lake Road, Meadville, PA 16335. The Meadville Plant comprises approximately 110,000 square feet of manufacturing and warehouse space situated on approximately 8.2 acres. CALDERWOOD & HARKNESS LLP Attorneys at Law
1114 Avenue of the Americas, 32nd Floor New York, New York 10036

Mr. Derek Amato General Counsel Crestline Packaging Solutions LLC 4100 Rockside Road, Suite 300 Independence, Ohio 44131
Dear Mr. Amato:
We are pleased that Crestline Packaging Solutions LLC ("Crestline" or the "Company"), a Delaware limited liability company, has selected Calderwood & Harkness LLP (the "Firm," "we," "us," or "our") to serve as its legal counsel in connection with the matter described below. We appreciate the confidence you and your team have placed in the Firm, and we look forward to providing the Company with excellent legal representation throughout the course of this engagement.
This letter (the "Engagement Letter") confirms that the Firm has been retained by Crestline to serve as buyer's counsel in connection with the proposed acquisition of substantially all of the assets comprising the ProShield Industrial Coatings product line (the "ProShield Product Line") from Voss Chemical Industries, Inc. ("Voss"), a New York corporation headquartered in Tonawanda, New York (the "Transaction"). The Transaction is anticipated to be structured as an asset purchase, with purchase price consideration expected to include both upfront cash consideration and a volume-based earnout component tied to post-closing gallons shipped over a twenty-four (24) month measurement period following the closing date. We understand that Crestline is a portfolio company of Kestrel Capital Partners Fund III, LP ("Fund III"). This engagement has been assigned Firm matter number 1006-00007, which should be referenced in all communications and payments directed to the Firm regarding this matter.
The purpose of this Engagement Letter is to set forth the terms and conditions governing the Firm's representation of Crestline in connection with the Transaction. We ask that you review this letter carefully and, if the terms are acceptable, that you countersign and return a copy to us in the manner indicated below.
1. Scope of Representation
The Firm will represent Crestline as buyer in all legal aspects of the proposed asset purchase of the ProShield Product Line from Voss, as more fully described below. The specific scope of our representation is anticipated to include the following:
(a) Transaction Structuring. Advising on and assisting with the structuring of the asset purchase transaction, including purchase price mechanics encompassing the allocation and structuring of upfront cash consideration, an escrow holdback to secure certain post-closing indemnification and purchase price adjustment obligations, and a volume-based earnout component linked to gallons of ProShield products shipped during the twenty-four (24) month post-closing measurement period.
(b) Legal Due Diligence. Conducting and coordinating comprehensive legal due diligence on the ProShield Product Line assets, which is expected to encompass, among other areas: Intellectual property rights (including trademarks, trade secrets, proprietary formulations, and know-how); customer contracts and supply agreements; employee and labor matters related to the ProShield Product Line; environmental matters (including compliance history, permits, and potential liabilities associated with the assets); and regulatory compliance matters relevant to the assets and the business of the ProShield Product Line.
(c) Transaction Documentation. Drafting, negotiating, and finalizing the definitive Asset Purchase Agreement (the "APA") and all ancillary transaction documents, including but not limited to the following:
(i) Bill of Sale;
(ii) Assignment and Assumption Agreement;
(iii) intellectual Property Assignment Agreement;
(iv) Escrow Agreement;
(v) Transition Services Agreement;
(vi) Non-Competition and Non-Solicitation Agreements applicable to Voss and its key principals;
(vii) Officer's Certificates and other customary closing certificates and deliverables; and
(viii) Such other ancillary agreements and instruments as may be necessary or appropriate to consummate the Transaction.
(d) Coordination with Advisors. Coordinating with Crestline's financial and accounting advisors, including Halcyon Chartered Accountants LLP, and Crestline's environmental consultants, including Northbridge Environmental Consulting Group LLC, regarding their respective workstreams and due diligence findings, in each case as they relate to the legal aspects of the Transaction.
(e) Indemnification and Escrow. Negotiating and structuring the indemnification framework set forth in the APA, including representations and warranties survival periods, indemnification baskets, caps, and other customary limitations, as well as coordinating the establishment and terms of the escrow arrangement with the designated escrow agent.
(f) Lender Coordination. Coordinating with Crestline's senior lender, Great Lakes Commerce Bank, N.A. (the "Lender"), regarding any required lender consents, waivers, or amendments to the Company's existing senior secured credit facility that may be necessary or advisable in connection with the financing and consummation of the Transaction.
(g) Representations and Warranties Insurance. Facilitating the procurement of a buyer-side representations and warranties insurance policy in connection with the Transaction, including coordinating with insurance brokers and underwriters, reviewing policy terms, and advising Crestline regarding coverage issues.
(h) Pre-Closing Conditions and Regulatory Matters. Advising on and assisting with the satisfaction of pre-closing conditions, including the analysis of the applicability of the Hart-Scott-Rodino Antitrust Improvements Act of 1976, as amended (the "HSR Act"), to the Transaction, the identification and procurement of any required third-party consents or governmental approvals, and the planning and coordination of closing mechanics.

MEMORANDUM
PRIVILEGED AND CONFIDENTIAL — ATTORNEY WORK PRODUCT
TO: Harrison Wexford, Partner, Calderwood & Harkness LLP Derek Amato, General Counsel, Crestline Packaging Solutions LLC
FROM: Ryan Kowalski, Lead Associate, and Megan Chu, Working Associate, Calderwood & Harkness LLP
DATE: October 28, 2022
RE: Summary of Key Legal Due Diligence Findings — Proposed Acquisition of ProShield Industrial Coatings Product Line from Voss Chemical Industries, Inc.
MATTER NO.: 1006-00007
Right-click to update Table of Contents
I. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
Calderwood & Harkness LLP ("C&H") has been retained by Crestline Packaging Solutions LLC ("Crestline" or "CPS"), a Delaware limited liability company headquartered at 4100 Rockside Road, Suite 300, Independence, OH 44131, as buyer's counsel in connection with the proposed asset purchase of substantially all assets comprising the ProShield Industrial Coatings product line (the "ProShield Product Line" or the "Business") from Voss Chemical Industries, Inc. ("Voss" or "VCI"), a New York corporation headquartered at 790 Niagara Falls Boulevard, Tonawanda, NY 14150 (the "Transaction").
Crestline is a portfolio company of Kestrel Capital Partners Fund III, LP, a Delaware limited partnership (GP: Cobalt Ridge Partners Management III, LLC) with its principal office at 200 Clarendon Street, 48th Floor, Boston, MA 02116 ("Ashgrove Equity Partners" or the "Sponsor"). The acquisition of the ProShield Product Line is part of Crestline's broader growth strategy to expand its specialty industrial coatings capabilities and customer base in the packaging and industrial end-markets, and has been approved by the Ashgrove Equity Partners investment committee, subject to satisfactory completion of all legal, financial, tax, and environmental due diligence.
The Transaction contemplates a base purchase price of $18,000,000, comprising $14,500,000 in cash payable at Closing, a $2,000,000 indemnification escrow (to be held by Pinnacle Trust Company, N.A. pursuant to a separate Escrow Agreement), and a volume-based earnout of up to $3,500,000 over a twenty-four (24) month measurement period following the Closing Date. The maximum total consideration payable by Crestline in connection with the Transaction is $20,000,000, assuming full achievement of all earnout milestones.
Legal due diligence commenced on October 10, 2022, following the execution of a binding Letter of Intent between the parties dated October 3, 2022. VCI and its counsel, Langford, Crewe & Cascade Insurance Brokers, have made available a virtual data room (hosted on Thackeray Solutions, Project Name "Vulcan") containing approximately 2,400 documents organized into 14 primary folders. This memorandum summarizes the findings and observations of C&H's legal due diligence review through October 28, 2022. Additional documents and supplemental responses to our diligence request list remain outstanding, and our review is ongoing. This memorandum will be updated as additional materials are received and analyzed.
In parallel with our legal review, the following advisors have been engaged by Crestline to conduct their respective workstreams:
•  Financial and Tax Due Diligence: Halcyon Chartered Accountants LLP (engagement partner Martin Szabo, CPA), 1301 East 9th Street, Suite 2400, Cleveland, OH 44114, is conducting financial quality-of-earnings and tax due diligence on the ProShield Product Line. Halcyon's preliminary findings have been shared with our legal team, and we are coordinating to ensure that financial observations are appropriately reflected in the representations, warranties, and disclosure schedules of the Asset Purchase Agreement.
•  Environmental Due Diligence: Northbridge Environmental Consulting Group LLC (project manager Aaron Lindquist, P.E.) has been engaged by Crestline to conduct a Phase I environmental site assessment of the Tonawanda manufacturing facility at 790 Niagara Falls Boulevard, Tonawanda, NY 14150. The Phase I report is expected by approximately November 4, 2022, and will inform our final recommendations on environmental risk allocation in the APA.
We note that the Hart-Scott-Rodino Antitrust Improvements Act of 1976, as amended (the "HSR Act"), does not require a pre-merger notification filing in connection with this Transaction. The total deal value of $18,000,000 (or $20,000,000 maximum with full earnout) falls below the applicable size-of-transaction reporting threshold currently in effect for calendar year 2022.
Overall Assessment. The ProShield Product Line presents a commercially attractive acquisition target for Crestline. The product line's revenue has grown consistently over the past three fiscal years (from $18.7M in FY2020 to an estimated $22.8M in FY2022), gross margins have improved from 38.2% to an estimated 40.0% over the same period, and the portfolio of 47 proprietary coating formulations provides meaningful competitive differentiation. However, our legal due diligence has identified several issues that require careful attention in APA drafting and negotiation, and which should inform the commercial terms of the Transaction. The key risk areas are as follows:
1.  Customer Contract Assignability / Change-of-Control Consent Requirements. Seven (7) of the twenty-three (23) active supply agreements included in the Transferred Assets contain anti-assignment or change-of-control consent provisions. Three (3) of these are among the top five (5) customer accounts by revenue, creating meaningful execution risk.
2.  Customer Concentration Risk. The top five (5) customer accounts represent approximately 58% of ProShield Product Line revenue, concentrating Crestline's post-Closing revenue base and, critically, the earnout measurement in a limited number of commercial relationships.
3.  Environmental Conditions at the Tonawanda Facility. While preliminary database searches have not identified the facility on any federal or state priority remediation lists, VCI's historical use of volatile organic compounds and solvents, together with the 2018 underground storage tank removal, warrant thorough environmental review. Final assessment is pending receipt of the Northbridge Phase I report.
4.  IP Chain-of-Title Completeness. Approximately eight (8) of the forty-seven (47) proprietary formulations were developed by former employees who signed only general employment agreements lacking specific invention assignment or work-for-hire clauses. Additionally, approximately five (5) formulations were co-developed with a raw material supplier under a joint development agreement that includes notice/consent requirements upon assignment or change of control.
5.  Employee Transition Mechanics. As an asset purchase, there is no automatic transfer of employment. Crestline will need to extend offers to thirty-four (34) product line employees, address restrictive covenant assignment issues, and manage the transition of personnel from VCI's benefit plans to Crestline's plans, all while preserving continuity of manufacturing operations and customer relationships.
Each of these issues is discussed in detail in the sections that follow, together with our recommendations for addressing them through the APA, ancillary agreements, and closing conditions.
II. CORPORATE ORGANIZATION AND AUTHORITY OF SELLER
A. Entity Status and Good Standing
Voss Chemical Industries, Inc. is a New York business corporation that was originally incorporated under the laws of the State of New York in 1987 by the Voss family. VCI has been continuously in existence since its date of incorporation and, based on our preliminary review, has maintained its corporate status in good standing throughout the relevant period. VCI's registered agent for service of process is Voss Chemical Industries, Inc., c/o Frederick Voss, 790 Niagara Falls Boulevard, Tonawanda, NY 14150. VCI's Employer Identification Number (EIN) is 16-2847103.
We have conducted a preliminary check with the New York Department of State, Division of Corporations, which confirms that VCI is currently in "active" status. Our review of available franchise tax filing records indicates that VCI is current on its New York State franchise tax obligations. As a closing deliverable, we recommend that the APA require Seller to deliver a current certificate of good standing (or equivalent certificate of status) from the New York Secretary of State, dated within ten (10) business days of the Closing Date. We will verify VCI's status again promptly prior to Closing.
VCI does not appear to be qualified as a foreign corporation in any state other than New York, although we have requested confirmation from Seller's counsel as to whether VCI has operations, employees, or property in any other jurisdiction that would require foreign qualification. This inquiry remains outstanding as of the date of this memorandum.

I. Executive Summary
This memorandum analyzes the federal, New York State, and Pennsylvania tax consequences of the proposed acquisition by Crestline Packaging Solutions LLC ("Crestline" or "CPS") of substantially all of the assets of Lakewood Regional Health Partners, LLC ("Lakewood" or "LRHP") for a fixed purchase price of One Hundred Forty Million Dollars ($140,000,000), structured as an asset purchase (the "Transaction"). The parties anticipate execution of the Asset Purchase Agreement (the "APA") on or about June 16, 2025, with an estimated Closing Date of August 15, 2025.
This memorandum addresses the following principal tax considerations arising from the Transaction:
(a) the federal income tax entity classification of both the Buyer (Crestline) and the Seller (Lakewood), including the consequences of Crestline's status as a disregarded entity and Lakewood's classification as a partnership;
(b) the inapplicability of an election under Section 338(h)(10) of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as amended (the "Code" or "IRC"), and the reasons why the asset purchase structure is both appropriate and optimal for the parties;

(e) bulk sale tax clearance requirements under New York Tax Law §1141(c) and analogous Pennsylvania requirements;
(f) the sales tax exemption analysis under the casual or isolated sale doctrine in both New York and Pennsylvania; and
(g) additional federal tax considerations, including assumed liabilities, transaction cost deductibility and capitalization, the pending Office of Inspector General ("OIG") inquiry at the Syracuse facility, and employee benefit plan transition matters.

The purpose of this memorandum is to document the decision to place Matter No. 1006-00003 on dormant status effective as of the date of this memorandum, November 4, 2022. This memorandum is intended to serve as a comprehensive record of the current state of the engagement and to provide a detailed framework for any future reactivation of the matter.

1.  Record the Background and Reason for Dormancy. Deal negotiations between Crestline Packaging Solutions LLC ("Crestline" or "CPS") and the shareholders of Allegheny Chemical Coatings, Inc. ("ACC" or the "Target") were paused on or about October 28, 2022, following unresolved disagreements regarding environmental liability escrow amounts and indemnification provisions in the draft Stock Purchase Agreement (the "SPA"). The parties have not formally terminated the transaction or the engagement; however, substantive work on the matter has ceased, and no further client instructions have been received.
2.  Identify All Outstanding and Incomplete Environmental Diligence Items. A number of critical environmental diligence work streams remain incomplete at the time of dormancy, most notably the Clarksburg Phase II Environmental Site Assessment analytical results and the finalization of the Comprehensive Environmental Diligence Summary Memorandum. Each outstanding item is identified and described in detail herein to ensure that nothing is overlooked in the event the matter is reactivated.
3.  Establish a Resumption Protocol for Reactivation of the Matter. This memorandum sets forth an eight-step protocol to be followed in the event that Crestline elects to resume negotiations and reactivate this engagement. The protocol is designed to ensure an orderly and efficient resumption of work and to address any developments that may have occurred during the dormancy period.
4.  Direct Preservation of All Work Product, Correspondence, and Electronic Files. All materials generated in connection with this engagement are subject to a document preservation directive issued concurrently with this memorandum. No documents, files, or electronic records relating to this matter shall be deleted, discarded, or destroyed until formal matter closure or resumption, as applicable.
This memorandum should be read in conjunction with the Environmental Diligence Status Tracker (last updated October 28, 2022, by Grace Nakamura), which serves as the master index of all diligence items, their current status, and responsible parties.
II. Engagement Background
A. The Transaction
Crestline Packaging Solutions LLC, an Ohio limited liability company headquartered at 4100 Riverside Commerce Drive, Suite 300, Dayton, OH 45402, is a wholly-owned portfolio company of Briarwood Capital Partners LP (Fund IV), a $2.1 billion private equity fund focused on middle-market industrial and specialty manufacturing investments. Crestline is a leading manufacturer and distributor of specialty packaging solutions serving the automotive, industrial, and consumer products sectors.
Crestline proposed to acquire one hundred percent (100%) of the outstanding common stock of Allegheny Chemical Coatings, Inc., a Pennsylvania corporation headquartered at 2200 Iron Works Boulevard, McKeesport, PA 15132, for a proposed purchase price of $94.5 million, calculated as $13.5 million of trailing twelve-month adjusted EBITDA at a 7.0x multiple. The transaction was structured as a stock purchase, with Crestline acquiring all outstanding shares of ACC common stock from the existing shareholders.
The proposed financing structure consisted of a $65 million senior secured term loan and a $20 million revolving credit facility from Commonwealth National Bank, N.A., pursuant to a commitment letter signed on July 8, 2022, together with a $9.5 million equity contribution from Briarwood Capital Partners Fund IV LP. The combined $94.5 million in sources was intended to fund the purchase price in full, exclusive of transaction costs.
The strategic rationale for the proposed acquisition centered on vertical integration of specialty coatings supply into Crestline's existing packaging operations. Management projections prepared by Crestline and validated by Briarwood's deal team estimated procurement cost savings of approximately $12 million to $15 million annually, to be realized over a three-year integration period, through the internalization of ACC's coating and resin formulation capabilities.
The ownership of ACC's outstanding common stock is divided among the following holders:
•  Walter Kessler, Founder and Chairman of the Board — 62%
•  Thomas Kessler, President and Chief Executive Officer — 18%
•  The Walter G. Kessler Revocable Trust — 12%
•  Allegheny Chemical Coatings, Inc. Employee Stock Ownership Plan — 8%
Seller's legal counsel in connection with the proposed transaction is Hargrove, Dalton & Speer LLP, Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, with Franklin Speer serving as lead partner. Seller's financial advisor is Veltrano Partners LLC, Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, with Nathan Ashford serving as managing director on the engagement.
The initial draft of the Stock Purchase Agreement was first circulated by Calderwood & Harkness LLP on behalf of Crestline on August 12, 2022. Revised drafts incorporating environmental representations and warranties, indemnification provisions, and related schedules and exhibits were exchanged between the parties through October 2022. Despite multiple rounds of negotiation, the SPA was never executed by the parties.
The original targeted closing date for the transaction was November 30, 2022, within the fourth quarter of 2022. The exclusivity period granted by the Seller pursuant to the Letter of Intent dated June 15, 2022, was set to expire on December 31, 2022. Following the pause in negotiations on or about October 28, 2022, the parties agreed informally to a standstill, with neither party affirmatively terminating the Letter of Intent or the exclusivity arrangement prior to its expiration.
B. The Environmental Diligence Engagement
Calderwood & Harkness LLP was engaged by Crestline Packaging Solutions LLC, through its General Counsel Derek Huang, to perform environmental due diligence services in connection with the proposed acquisition of ACC. The engagement was formalized pursuant to an engagement letter dated July 19, 2022, executed by Mr. Huang on behalf of Crestline and by the undersigned on behalf of Calderwood & Harkness LLP. The matter was opened under Matter No. 1006-00003.
The scope of the engagement, as defined in the engagement letter, encompassed the following principal workstreams:
(i) Oversight and review of Phase I and Phase II Environmental Site Assessments conducted by TerraVerde Environmental Consulting LLC ("TerraVerde") at ACC's four operating facilities;
(ii) Review of environmental permits, compliance history, and regulatory filings for each of ACC's four facilities, including RCRA, Clean Air Act, Clean Water Act, EPCRA/TRI, and applicable state environmental program filings;
(iii) Analysis of environmental representations, warranties, and indemnification provisions in the draft Stock Purchase Agreement, including review of Seller's disclosure schedules and negotiation of revisions thereto;
(iv) Negotiation of environmental risk allocation provisions, including environmental escrow, indemnification caps and baskets, survival periods, and related deal mechanics;
(v) Evaluation of Pollution Legal Liability ("PLL") insurance options as a potential mechanism for bridging environmental risk allocation gaps between the parties; and
(vi) Preparation of a comprehensive environmental diligence summary memorandum for delivery to the client and its financial sponsor.

Calderwood & Harkness LLP ("C&H" or the "Firm") is pleased to confirm the engagement by Vantage Mobility Systems Corp., a Delaware corporation ("VMS," the "Company," or the "Client"), to serve as legal counsel to VMS in connection with the matters described herein. This engagement shall be effective as of March 28, 2022.
We understand that VMS is a portfolio company of Ridgepoint Capital Partners, LP ("Ridgepoint"), a Delaware limited partnership, and that VMS is currently held in Ridgepoint Capital Fund II, LP (vintage 2017). We wish to clarify at the outset that our client in this engagement is VMS and not Ridgepoint, Ridgepoint Capital Fund II, LP, Ridgepoint Capital GP II, LLC, or any other Ridgepoint affiliate. Grasso (the "Bankruptcy Case"). The Bankruptcy Case is currently pending, and we understand that the Debtor, through its counsel, Hargrove Tillinghast LLP, has initiated a process to solicit stalking-horse bids for the sale of substantially all of the Debtor's assets.

The acquisition is expected to be conducted through a sale process under Section 363 of the Bankruptcy Code, subject to higher and better offers at auction and approval by the Bankruptcy Court.
Collectively, the foregoing proposed transaction and all related proceedings, negotiations, filings, and activities shall be referred to herein as the "Matter."

This memorandum is submitted to the Managing Partner's Office and the New Business Committee of Calderwood & Harkness LLP in connection with the opening of a new client matter. The purpose of this memorandum is to provide the Committee with all information necessary to evaluate and approve the firm's representation of Meridian Consumer Brands LLC in the transaction described herein, and to establish the administrative, billing, and staffing framework for the engagement. All information contained herein is strictly confidential and is subject to the firm's internal information barriers and confidentiality policies.
1. Matter Summary
Client: Meridian Consumer Brands LLC, a Delaware limited liability company, with its principal place of business located at 440 Park Avenue South, 18th Floor, New York, NY 10016. The client's federal Employer Identification Number is 83-2947106.
Matter Type: Asset Purchase (Mergers & Acquisitions)
Description of Engagement: Calderwood & Harkness LLP ("C&H" or the "Firm") has been engaged to serve as buyer's counsel to Meridian Consumer Brands LLC ("Meridian" or "MCB" or the "Client") in connection with a proposed asset purchase transaction valued at approximately $95,000,000. The transaction involves the acquisition by Meridian of the "CleanLeaf" branded home cleaning product line and the "PureHaven" branded personal care product line (collectively, the "Acquired Product Lines" or the "Acquired Assets") from Briarwood Home Essentials, Inc. ("Briarwood" or "BHE"), an Ohio corporation headquartered at 1175 Creekside Drive, Suite 400, Columbus, OH 43215 (EIN: 31-1684239). Briarwood is a privately held consumer products company whose sole shareholder is Malcolm Greer.
The parties executed a Letter of Intent on March 28, 2022, which sets forth the principal terms of the proposed transaction on a non-binding basis (with certain binding provisions relating to exclusivity, confidentiality, governing law, and dispute resolution). Due diligence is scheduled to formally commence on June 14, 2022, through a virtual data room hosted on the Pemberton Systems platform.
Governing Law: The transaction will be governed by the laws of the State of New York, consistent with the governing law provisions of the Letter of Intent and the anticipated Asset Purchase Agreement.
Engagement Letter: An engagement letter has been executed concurrently with this memorandum on June 10, 2022, and is addressed to Diana Ressler, General Counsel, Meridian Consumer Brands LLC. A copy of the executed engagement letter is maintained in the matter file. The engagement letter sets forth the scope of the Firm's representation, the applicable fee arrangements, and the terms and conditions of the attorney-client relationship.

Full Legal Name: Meridian Consumer Brands LLC
Short Name / Matter Alias: Meridian / MCB

Federal Employer Identification Number (EIN): 83-2947106
Client Background: Meridian Consumer Brands LLC is a portfolio company of Lakepoint Capital Partners, LP, a mid-market private equity fund based in Boston, Massachusetts. Meridian was formed in 2017 as a purpose-built acquisition vehicle for the consolidation and operation of consumer brands in the household cleaning, laundry, and personal care segments. Since its formation, Meridian has successfully acquired, integrated, and operated five distinct consumer brands spanning these categories.
Meridian's combined annual revenues across its existing brand portfolio are approximately $620 million, and the company employs over 1,800 individuals across manufacturing, distribution, marketing, and corporate functions in multiple states. Meridian has completed three prior bolt-on acquisitions since its formation, all of which were structured as asset purchases or membership interest purchases. The proposed acquisition of the CleanLeaf and PureHaven product lines from Briarwood represents Meridian's fourth bolt-on acquisition and is consistent with its stated growth strategy of acquiring complementary, eco-friendly consumer product brands with strong retail distribution channels.
Calderwood & Harkness LLP has not previously represented Meridian Consumer Brands LLC. This engagement represents a new client relationship for the Firm. Dear Diana:
I am writing on behalf of Calderwood & Harkness LLP in connection with the proposed $95,000,000 asset purchase by Meridian Consumer Brands LLC ("Meridian" or the "Company") of the CleanLeaf and PureHaven consumer product lines (collectively, the "Product Lines") from Briarwood Home Essentials, Inc. ("Briarwood"). The purpose of this letter is threefold: (1) to provide you and your team with a comprehensive update on the current dormant status of the transaction, (2) to identify a number of time-sensitive issues that require the Company's prompt attention, and (3) to outline the strategic options available to Meridian at this juncture.
As you are aware, the last substantive negotiation call between the parties took place on November 18, 2022. Since that call, the only communication between deal counsel was a scheduling proposal sent by our associate, Naomi Petersen, to David Soo at Caldwell, Pruitt & Shaw LLP on December 9, 2022, proposing dates for a follow-up discussion. That email received no response. No formal termination of the Letter of Intent ("LOI") or the Asset Purchase Agreement ("APA") negotiations has occurred, and neither party has communicated a decision to abandon the transaction. As a practical matter, however, the transaction has been effectively dormant since mid-December 2022.
For the reasons set forth in detail below, we recommend that Meridian make a decision on the path forward by no later than mid-February 2023. Several impending deadlines — most critically, the expiration of the Harborview National Bank debt commitment letter on February 5, 2023 — make continued inaction increasingly costly and strategically inadvisable. We address each of the relevant issues in turn.
1. Debt Commitment Letter Expiration — Harborview National Bank, N.A.
The senior secured term loan commitment letter (the "Commitment Letter") between Meridian and Harborview National Bank, N.A. ("Harborview"), providing for a $60,000,000 senior secured term loan facility, was executed on August 5, 2022. Meridian's relationship manager at Harborview is Carolyn Dubois, Senior Vice President, Leveraged Finance. The Commitment Letter was the product of an approximately three-month negotiation process and represented a key milestone in establishing the financing architecture for the proposed acquisition.
By its express terms, the Commitment Letter expires on February 5, 2023 — approximately sixteen (16) days from the date of this letter.
The principal economic terms of the committed facility, as set forth in the Commitment Letter and the accompanying term sheet, include the following:
•  Interest Rate: Secured Overnight Financing Rate (SOFR) plus 375 basis points, with a 50 basis point SOFR floor;
•  Commitment Fee: 50 basis points per annum on undrawn committed amounts, payable quarterly in arrears;
•  Ticking Fee: 25 basis points on the total committed amount, commencing 90 days after the date of the Commitment Letter (as discussed further in Section 2 below); and
•  Syndication: The facility was structured to include Pinnacle Credit Partners, LP (contact: Rajan Mehta, Managing Director) as a syndicate participant, with Harborview acting as administrative agent and sole lead arranger.
Upon expiration of the Commitment Letter, Meridian will have no committed debt financing in place for the transaction. If Meridian subsequently determines that it wishes to proceed with the acquisition of the Product Lines, new financing arrangements would need to be negotiated from scratch. While we cannot predict future credit market conditions, we note that the current interest rate environment has shifted meaningfully since August 2022, and any new commitment obtained in the first quarter of 2023 or thereafter could entail materially different — and potentially less favorable — pricing terms, tighter covenants, or reduced lender appetite for leveraged acquisition financing in the consumer products sector.

Dear Mr. Ostrander:

Calderwood & Harkness LLP ("C&H," "we," or the "Firm") is pleased to confirm that Brightfield Cloud Services Inc., a Delaware corporation ("BCS" or the "Company"), has engaged the Firm to serve as outside legal counsel to BCS in connection with BCS's proposed acquisition of Codelaunch Labs, Inc., a Delaware corporation ("Codelaunch" or the "Target"), with principal offices located in Austin, Texas. We appreciate the Company's confidence in retaining us for this matter and look forward to working with you and your team throughout the course of this transaction.
As we understand it based on our preliminary discussions, BCS proposes to acquire the Target through a forward merger, with aggregate merger consideration of approximately Twenty-Two Million Dollars ($22,000,000) payable in cash at closing (subject to customary adjustments and any earnout consideration to be agreed upon during negotiations). The specific terms of the acquisition will be documented in a definitive Agreement and Plan of Merger and related ancillary agreements, all of which will be subject to negotiation with Codelaunch and its counsel.
This engagement letter (this "Letter") sets forth the scope of our representation, the staffing of the engagement team, the fee arrangements applicable to our services, and the standard terms and conditions governing the Firm's representation of BCS in connection with this matter. We ask that you review this Letter carefully and, if the terms are acceptable, execute and return a copy to our office to confirm BCS's agreement to the terms set forth herein.

(c) Leading the negotiation of the definitive Agreement and Plan of Merger on behalf of BCS with Codelaunch's counsel, including all substantive provisions relating to the merger consideration (including any purchase price adjustments tied to working capital, cash, indebtedness, or transaction expenses of the Target), earnout mechanics (if applicable), representations and warranties of the Target and BCS, pre-closing covenants, closing conditions, indemnification provisions (including negotiation of the cap, basket or deductible, tipping versus true deductible structure, survival periods for representations and warranties, and special indemnity provisions as warranted), and escrow arrangements for indemnification claims;

(e) Preparing, reviewing, and finalizing all drafts of the Agreement and Plan of Merger, mark-ups, and related negotiation correspondence.

MEMORANDUM
PRIVILEGED AND CONFIDENTIAL — ATTORNEY-CLIENT COMMUNICATION / ATTORNEY WORK PRODUCT
TO: Patricia Yamamoto, General Counsel, Arbor Health Technologies Inc. Derek Huang, Chief Compliance Officer, Arbor Health Technologies Inc.
FROM: Miriam Calloway, Partner, Calderwood & Harkness LLP Christopher Aiken, Senior Associate, Calderwood & Harkness LLP Amy Whitfield, Associate, Calderwood & Harkness LLP
DATE: April 10, 2023
RE: Post-Acquisition Compliance Gap Assessment — Lakeview Medical Associates, P.C. Legacy Arrangements
MATTER NO.: 1010-00003
Right-click to update Table of Contents
I. Executive Summary
Arbor Health Technologies Inc. ("AHT") has engaged Calderwood & Harkness LLP to conduct a comprehensive compliance gap assessment of the physician compensation arrangements, medical director agreements, and office leases assumed by AHT in connection with its acquisition of substantially all assets of Lakeview Medical Associates, P.C. ("Lakeview"). The purpose of this memorandum is to identify specific compliance gaps arising under the federal Anti-Kickback Statute, 42 U.S.C. § 1320a-7b(b) (the "AKS"), and the Physician Self-Referral Law, 42 U.S.C. § 1395nn (the "Stark Law"), and to set forth remediation recommendations with associated timelines and priority classifications.
The acquisition of Lakeview's assets closed on August 15, 2022, at an asset purchase price of $11.4 million. The transaction was handled by Westbrook Hale LLP (Elena Marchetti, partner) as AHT's general outside counsel. Importantly, healthcare regulatory due diligence in connection with the transaction was limited in scope. Westbrook Hale expressly deferred to Calderwood & Harkness LLP on healthcare regulatory and compliance aspects, but Calderwood & Harkness was not engaged for pre-closing due diligence and was retained only post-closing pursuant to AHT Board Resolution No. 2023-01-004, adopted January 24, 2023.
This memorandum covers the following legacy Lakeview arrangements assumed by AHT at closing:
•  Fourteen (14) physician agreements, consisting of twelve (12) W-2 employed physician agreements and two (2) independent contractor agreements, spanning multiple specialties including primary care, orthopedics, gastroenterology, and cardiology;
•  Three (3) medical director agreements, with annual stipends of $45,000, $60,000, and $72,000, respectively (aggregate annual stipend obligation of $177,000); and
•  Two (2) office leases for clinic space at 75 Belmont Street, Worcester, MA 01605 (the "Worcester Clinic") and 310 Main Street, Suite 2A, Shrewsbury, MA 01545 (the "Shrewsbury Clinic").
This memorandum is part of the broader self-assessment engagement authorized by AHT Board Resolution No. 2023-01-004 and cross-references the gap assessment report prepared by Grayson Whitaker & Associates LLP (report reference: GW-AHT-2022-Final, dated December 12, 2022, prepared under the direction of Carolyn Fitch, Principal). The Grayson Whitaker report identified several Lakeview legacy arrangements among its seventeen (17) "high-risk" and twenty-three (23) "moderate-risk" findings across AHT's portfolio of healthcare arrangements.
The compliance significance of the Lakeview arrangements is heightened by the scale of Lakeview's participation in federal healthcare programs. Prior to the acquisition, Lakeview's annual revenue was approximately $18.2 million, of which approximately $10.9 million (approximately 60%) was attributable to Medicare and Medicaid reimbursement. This substantial federal healthcare program participation subjects all Lakeview physician compensation arrangements, medical director agreements, and office leases to full scrutiny under both the Stark Law and the AKS.
Key Finding: Our review has identified multiple compliance gaps across the Lakeview legacy arrangements. These gaps include, but are not limited to: (i) the absence of contemporaneous fair market value ("FMV") substantiation for physician compensation, medical director stipends, and rental rates; (ii) expired agreement terms creating holdover arrangements with informal, undocumented modifications that undermine compliance with applicable Stark Law exceptions and AKS safe harbors; (iii) compensation formulas in physician employment agreements that fail to satisfy the Stark Law requirement that compensation not be determined in a manner that takes into account the volume or value of referrals; (iv) vague and non-specific duty descriptions in medical director agreements that undermine commercial reasonableness defenses; and (v) writing requirement gaps arising from informal modifications to compensation terms during holdover periods. Critically, several of these gaps existed at the time of the acquisition and were carried forward post-closing when AHT assumed the arrangements without amendment.

I. Executive Summary
The purpose of this memorandum is to summarize the key findings of the legal due diligence review conducted by Calderwood & Harkness LLP on behalf of our client, Lumos Analytics Inc. ("Lumos" or the "Buyer"), in connection with the proposed acquisition of Prismyx Data Solutions LLC ("Prismyx" or the "Target"). The proposed transaction is structured as a forward merger under Section 18-209 of the Delaware Limited Liability Company Act (the "DLLCA"), pursuant to which Prismyx Acquisition Sub LLC, a newly formed Delaware limited liability company and wholly owned subsidiary of Lumos (the "Merger Sub"), will serve as the merger subsidiary. Under the merger structure, Prismyx will merge with and into Merger Sub, with Merger Sub surviving as a wholly owned subsidiary of Lumos.
The due diligence review was conducted during the period from March 4, 2024 through March 29, 2024. During this period, the diligence team reviewed materials provided by Prismyx and its outside counsel, Cartwright, Daugherty & Voss LLP (Sabrina Delvecchio, lead partner; Marcus Greenbaum, associate), through a virtual data room hosted on Thackeray Solutions. In addition to the data room materials, the diligence team reviewed publicly available records, filings with the Delaware Secretary of State, records maintained by the United States Patent and Trademark Office ("USPTO"), and the results of Uniform Commercial Code ("UCC") and lien searches conducted in the states of Delaware and Pennsylvania.
Overall Assessment. Prismyx presents a relatively clean diligence profile, consistent with expectations for an early-stage software-as-a-service ("SaaS") company of its size and maturity. The Target's organizational structure is straightforward, its capitalization table is simple, and its regulatory footprint is minimal. We did not identify any material litigation, regulatory investigations, or undisclosed liabilities that would constitute a "deal-breaker" or fundamentally alter the economics of the proposed transaction. That said, the diligence review identified several risk areas that warrant attention in the definitive transaction documents and in integration planning, the most significant of which are as follows:
(a) Customer Concentration. Prismyx's revenue base is concentrated among a small number of customers, with the top three customers accounting for approximately 61% of total 2023 revenue.

### 2.1 Nexford Industrial Holdings Inc. — Pinnacle Metal Fabricators LLC (Matter 1005-00006)
- **Sponsor.** The engagement letter (July 11, 2023), APA recitals and closing checklist identify Nexford as \"a portfolio company of Bramblewood Capital Partners, LP\". Bramblewood holds about 78% through its ~$1.2B Fund III and bought the platform in 2019 for about $190M EV. Deal partner and board observer: Catherine E. Moreau.
- **Deal.**
  - Acquisition of substantially all assets of an Indiana custom metal fabricator: ~$18.4M revenue, $3.7M adj. EBITDA, 74 employees.
  - Price: $30M total, made up of $24M closing cash (of which $3M went to escrow at Commonwealth Escrow Services) plus up to $6M earnout in two $3M tranches tied to EBITDA targets of $4.2M and $4.8M.
  - Implied multiple: ~8.1x total / 6.5x cash.
  - Funding: $20M revolver draw (Greystone National Bank, which consented under §7.04 of the A&R credit agreement) plus $4M cash.
  - R&W policy from Sentinel Specialty.
  - No HSR filing required ($30M is below the $111.4M threshold).
- **Timeline.** LOI and engagement July 11, 2023; APA Sept. 5, 2023; closed Oct. 24, 2023.
- **Add-on characterization.** The deal summary memo calls it \"the fifth tuck-in acquisition completed by Nexford since Bramblewood's acquisition of the platform in 2019 … consistent with Nexford's disciplined buy-and-build strategy.\"

### 2.10 Lumos Analytics Inc. — Prismyx Data Solutions LLC (Matter 1008-00008)
- **Sponsor.** The 1008-00008 documents do not themselves name a sponsor. Lumos's other matters describe it as sponsor-backed, but they disagree on who the sponsor is:
  - 1008-00001 deal summary: \"Lumos is a portfolio company of Verdant Capital Partners Fund III, L.P.\" (a growth-equity fund; \"Sponsor / Majority Equity Holder\"; change-of-control tied to Verdant holding 25% or more).
  - Another Lumos document: \"majority equity holder is Ridgeline Capital Partners, LP, a private equity firm\" (Series C, 2021).
  - Several engagement letters: \"portfolio company of Pinnacle Venture Fund II LP.\"
  - Lumos has also done a SAFE round (1008-00003) and a withdrawn S-1 (1008-00002).
- **Treatment.** Included because Lumos is described as a sponsor-controlled portfolio company and the 1008-00001 credit facility was negotiated specifically to allow \"tuck-in acquisitions.\" **Flag: confirm with the relationship partner whether Lumos counts as \"PE-backed\" (rather than VC/growth-backed) for this review.**
- **Deal.**
  - Forward merger into Prismyx Acquisition Sub LLC for $15M total deal value: $10.5M closing cash, of which a $4.5M escrow is held at Fenwick, plus up to $4.5M earnout (two ARR-based tranches).
  - Funded through Linden Grove National Bank.
- **Timeline.** Engagement Feb. 20, 2024; merger agreement Apr. 3, 2024; closed May 27, 2024.
- **Documents relied on:**

  - Diligence/due-diligence-memo.docx

## 4. Data-integrity flags for the review

1. **Sponsor identities are inconsistent across matters for the same client.** Use each matter's own documents (as in Section 2) and confirm current ownership with the client teams before relying on any sponsor attribution.
   - **Crestline:**
     - Briarwood Capital Partners Fund IV (2022, ACC)
     - Kestrel Capital Partners Fund III / \"Ashgrove\" (2022, ProShield)
     - Ridgeway Capital Partners Fund III (2025, AVP)
     - Pinnacle River Capital Partners via CPS Holdings (2025, Lakewood)
     - Thornfield Capital Partners as equity sponsor (Ch. 11 matter 1006-00002)
   - **Nexford:** Bramblewood (1005-00006); Granite Peak Capital Partners (1005-00002 / 1005-00001); Veltrano Capital Partners (1005-00003).
   - **VMS:** Ridgepoint (2022); Veltrano Capital Partners Fund IV (2025); Northgate Capital Partners, Ironclad Capital Partners and Ashgrove are also named in other VMS files.
   - **MCB:** Lakepoint (1011-00005); Brindoval and Briarstone are named elsewhere.

input.message:
I found 10 add-on (bolt-on) acquisitions where one of our PE-sponsor-backed portfolio-company clients was the buyer and the firm acted as buyer's counsel. Seven closed and three did not. Everything is written up in `/workspace/output/response.md`, the only file in /workspace/output; I checked it after writing (about 3,570 words).

**Closed (about $440M in total):**

| Matter | Buyer | Target | Value | Closed |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1005-00006 | Nexford Industrial Holdings | Pinnacle Metal Fabricators (assets) | $30M, including $6M earnout | Oct 24, 2023 |
| 1006-00007 | Crestline Packaging | Voss Chemical's ProShield product line | $18M base, up to $20M | Jan 20, 2023 |
| 1006-00006 | Crestline Packaging | Allegheny Valley Packaging (assets) | $180M | Jul 31, 2025 |
| 1006-00008 | Crestline Packaging | Lakewood Regional Health Partners (assets) | $140M | Aug 15, 2025 |
| 1007-00006 | Vantage Mobility Systems | PulseLink Telematics (stock) | $35M | Jun 13, 2025 |
| 1042-00004 | Brightfield Cloud Services | Codelaunch Labs (merger) | $22M | Jul 22, 2023 |
| 1008-00008 | Lumos Analytics | Prismyx Data Solutions (merger) | $15M | May 27, 2024 |

**Did not close (about $253M):**
- **1006-00003, Crestline / Allegheny Chemical Coatings ($94.5M):** the firm handled only the environmental diligence. Talks paused in October 2022, the purchase agreement was never signed, and the matter went dormant.
- **1007-00002, Vantage Mobility / Meridian Precision Components ($63.5M):** a bankruptcy-sale stalking-horse bid. The court postponed the auction indefinitely on July 18, 2022.
- **1011-00005, Meridian Consumer Brands / CleanLeaf and PureHaven product lines ($95M):** went dormant in late 2022. The debt commitment and exclusivity both lapsed in early 2023.

**Things the partner should know:**
- **Lumos may not belong on the list.** Its files describe it variously as backed by a growth-equity fund, a PE firm or a venture fund. I included Prismyx but flagged it for confirmation.
- **Sponsor names conflict across matters for the same client.** For example, Crestline is tied to four or five different sponsors depending on the matter, and Nexford, Vantage Mobility, Meridian and Brightfield have similar conflicts. The memo attributes each deal to the sponsor named in that matter's own documents and asks the client teams to confirm.
- **The PulseLink documents carry the wrong matter number.** They say 1001-00004, which belongs to an Ardent Capital matter, but they sit in folder 1007-00006.
- **Lakewood is a physician group, not a packaging business.** The files describe it as part of Crestline's healthcare-division bolt-on strategy, so I counted it, but it is outside the platform's core business.

The memo also lists add-ons by these clients that appear in our files but where we weren't deal counsel, such as Nexford's four earlier bolt-ons and its $138M Kessler deal. Another is Arbor Health's $11.4M Lakeview acquisition, on which we did only post-closing compliance work. It ends with the deals I excluded and why: the buyer was the fund itself (Ardent, Harrowgate, Solara), a public or non-PE-backed company, or the matter wasn't an acquisition of a business.

To find these, I converted all ~9,300 documents to text and identified each matter's client. I then searched for acquisition language and read the key engagement, deal-summary, closing and status documents for each candidate. I did not read every file in full; long purchase agreements and diligence memos were checked only for the specific facts used.

Files in /workspace/output:
- response.md
